summary: Round 4 re-confirm. The geometry is unchanged and report.json has no problems: every requirement passes (twr 2.11, twr_sag 1.90 from the catalog motors, mass 769.9 / 790 g, CG 0.30 mm), all FEA cases pass at SF 3 including the new single-shear pin moments, the sweeps are clear, and holewall raises no insert-wall warning. But the new per-object print settings in the plate 3MFs are missing for 4 of the 9 parts: kerf/export.py _write_part_settings reads only the first 200 kB of 3D/3dmodel.model, so every object tag past that point is dropped. motor_hub and leg_1, both strength-checked and both meant to print at 4 walls, will slice at the printer defaults. The plate files contradict PRINT_SETTINGS.md and the design's own strength and insert-wall assumptions.

findings.issue: Metadata/model_settings.config is missing objects. plate_1 has gimbal_outer but not leg_1 (its object tag is at byte 641575). plate_2 has leg_2, leg_3 and ring_low but not motor_hub (byte 1329357). plate_3 has ring_top but not ring_mid (byte 407916) or motor_plate (byte 1417221). Cause: `head = files[model][:200000]` in _write_part_settings only regex-scans the first 200 kB of the model XML, so any object after a large mesh is skipped. As a result motor_hub (all thrust, 3 M3 inserts; meant to be 50 % / 4 walls) and leg_1 (crash-loaded; 25 % / 4 walls) slice at the printer defaults (typically 15 % / 2 walls = 0.84 mm, under the 1.6 mm insert wall the design relies on). ring_mid and motor_plate lose their 30 % / 50 % infill. Opening the plate files gives no sign of this. It would hit every project's plates.
findings.fix: Scan the whole model XML for object tags (drop the 200 kB cap, or stream it with iterparse and stop at <build>), or take the object ids from the mesher that writes the plate. Add a test with a multi-object plate whose second object starts past 200 kB, and assert that every object id gets an entry. Rebuild.

findings.issue: The new holewall check warns that the MG90S tab taps (79 % material at 1.5 d, groups yoke_servo and ring_servo) and the motor M3 counterbores on the 16 mm bolt circle (88 %, groups hub_motor_top and plate_motor_bottom) are under the s7 edge distance. The warning asks for this to be stated in DESIGN.md, and it is not.
findings.fix: Add one line: the edge distance is set by the purchased MG90S tab and 2207 16 x 16 hole patterns. The tabs have 2.4 mm of wall plus 4 perimeters; the motor holes are under 3 mm clamp with a 2 mm motor-base engagement.

findings.issue: FEA is run on a solid model, but ring_low now prints at 20 % infill (was 40 %). The 8 mm lug plate is roughly two 1 mm skins and 4 perimeters around a 20 % core, so its bending stiffness and strength are well under solid. lug_fea, the tightest case at 7.88 vs 13 MPa (z), could lose most of its SF 3 margin in reality. Same caveat for gimbal_outer at 20 %.
findings.fix: Add a slicer modifier (100 % or >= 50 % infill) over the three leg lugs and ribs, or print ring_low at 40 % (about +10 g, within the 790 g budget). Note it in PRINT_SETTINGS / DESIGN.

findings.issue: Carried over: 14 first-layer edges cannot be chamfered (deburr warning).
findings.fix: Deburr after printing, or use slicer elephant-foot compensation.

findings.issue: Carried over: leg_fea deflection is 2.966 vs 3.0 mm (99 %); accepted.
